answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require verifiable proof of history: each agent earns a reputation ledger over time, like crystal forming layer by layer, instead of spawning instantly. New identities start with near-zero trust and must complete real, attested tasks before touching shared resources. An ocean of cheap copies cannot overwhelm a system anchored to basalt-solid, checkable track records, because the cost of each identity grows with the trust it wants to claim.
